title: Chair Screen and Pop
description: A screener sets a legal, stationary chair screen for a teammate, who reads the defense to decide between curling to the rim and popping out for a shot.

content.objective: Set a solid, fully stationary chair screen, then read whether to curl or pop off it.
content.setup: A screener sets up at the elbow; a cutter starts at the block.
instructions: The screener gets the chair fully stopped and set at the elbow before any contact.
The cutter pushes tight off the screen, brushing close to the screener's chair.
If the defender trails, the cutter curls directly to the rim.
If the defender goes under, the cutter pops out to the wing for a catch-and-shoot instead.
coachingPoints: The screener must be fully stopped before contact — a moving screen is a foul.
The cutter should read the defender's path, not guess.
Change pushing rhythm off the screen to create real separation.
commonMistakes: Screening while the chair is still moving.
Cutter drifting too far from the screen, giving the defender room to recover.
Crowding a teammate's space instead of keeping good spacing.
content.safety: The screener holds a legal, fully stationary position — no moving into contact.
